hypothesis.text: Arkansas can sustainably retain and attract households and productive capital—especially into smaller communities—by building a Distributed Prosperity Network of authentic regional engines connected by excellent education, healthcare, broadband, housing, childcare, safety, civic life, ownership pathways, and opportunity, such that residual wealth contribution and anti-avoidance rules operate inside a society people choose, rather than a jurisdiction they try to escape.
hypothesis.central_question: What combination of infrastructure, services, opportunity, ownership, taxation, civic life, and quality of place causes households and productive capital to remain in, return to, and move into Arkansas—especially its smaller communities?
hypothesis.permanence_question: Which interventions actually produce permanent households rather than temporary relocations?
hypothesis.constitutional_capitalism_test: Can CC turn population and capital attraction into a measured prosperity engine—Keep / Return / Attract—without coercing mobility, inventing migration elasticities, or converting rootedness credits into loopholes?

governance.reason: Steve-directed core population-and-capital strategy linking residual wealth sustainability, Distributed Prosperity Network (HYP-124), strategic capacity (HYP-130), and public-income engines (HYP-131). Registration only — no migration microsim or amenity census executed.

strategic_posture.wealth_rule: No loopholes for wealth already subject to Arkansas law—but make Arkansas so desirable, productive, connected, and family-friendly that leaving is economically and personally unattractive
strategic_posture.mobility_rule: No loopholes does not mean no mobility; ordinary residency, nexus, beneficial ownership, realization, and anti-avoidance must survive legal review
strategic_posture.migration_evidence_posture: MIXED — some research finds limited high-earner migration response to state taxes; other work finds meaningful responses among highly mobile groups (e.g. star scientists). Do not lock a single elasticity.

migration_citations_research_only.label: Behavioral Responses to State Income Taxation of High Earners (NBER w26349)
The Effect of State Taxes on the Geographical Location of Star Scientists (NBER w21120)
migration_citations_research_only.use: Highly mobile talent can respond in some contexts — attraction strategy required

keep.name: Keep
keep.definition: Stop losing young families and skilled people

return.name: Return
return.definition: Create reasons for Arkansans who left for college or careers to come home

attract.name: Attract
attract.definition: Recruit families, entrepreneurs, skilled workers, researchers, professionals, remote workers, and eventually capital from other states

population_goals.composition_rule: A county gaining retirees is different from one gaining 30-year-old families with children — age/income/wealth/family composition must be measured separately

distributed_prosperity_network.rule: Reject the idea that economic opportunity requires moving everyone toward Little Rock or Northwest Arkansas
distributed_prosperity_network.access_standard: Every Arkansan should be able to reach excellent education, healthcare, broadband, employment, culture, recreation, food, transportation, and civic life without needing to live in a major urban center
distributed_prosperity_network.specialization_rule: Not every town becomes identical; every region develops a prosperity engine authentic to it
distributed_prosperity_network.connect_all: Physical and digital connections among specialized hubs

regional_prosperity_hubs.definition: Places or networks (e.g. 15,000; 3,000; or five-town networks) with access to healthcare, education, trades, broadband, food, emergency services, capital, housing, civic life, and transportation
regional_prosperity_hubs.state_investment_rule: Major state investment must consider whether it can strengthen a smaller community or regional hub before defaulting to an existing metropolitan concentration
regional_prosperity_hubs.not: Artificially suppressing Little Rock or Northwest Arkansas

family_attraction_package.value_proposition: People should not move to rural Arkansas merely to consume cheaper housing — they should see a pathway toward ownership and long-term wealth

remote_work_posture.rule: Remote workers can help seed population growth, but remote work alone cannot rebuild a community
remote_work_posture.rural_migration_evidence_posture: USDA ERS: nonmetro population growth since 2020 from migration offsetting natural decrease; recent domestic migration mixed; remote-rural counties still face structural demographic challenges

broadband_existing_program.name: Arkansas Rural Connect (ARC) / State Broadband Office
broadband_existing_program.note: Not starting from zero — program existence bound as secondary; coverage/outcomes NEE

cash_incentive_experiments.posture: Recruitment experiments, not proof of durable community renewal
cash_incentive_experiments.example_secondary: Rural relocation cash/internet stipends elsewhere can generate applicant interest — durability unproven

population_as_prosperity_engine.model_required: Lifetime fiscal and economic value of attracting a household — by type (young family vs retiree vs remote worker vs entrepreneur)
population_as_prosperity_engine.investment_justification: Housing, broadband, schools, childcare, healthcare, downtowns, parks, local business development as productive population infrastructure — not mere amenities

entrepreneurship_retention.pitch: You can build extraordinary wealth here—and your family can build an extraordinary life here

social_contract_with_wealth.not: We are going to punish rich people
social_contract_with_wealth.is: Arkansas wants you to build wealth here, invest here, raise children here, employ people here, innovate here, and become part of the community. In return, once you possess extraordinary surplus wealth, you contribute a small share toward maintaining the society that makes that prosperity possible.
social_contract_with_wealth.protection_clarity: Ordinary labor and ordinary homeownership are protected by the residual-wealth universal floor — the bargain is understandable

arkansas_rootedness.purpose: Study whether verified Arkansas investment should receive credits against some forms of future residual wealth contribution, provided the investment creates measurable Arkansas public capacity
arkansas_rootedness.not: A popularity discount or unstructured loophole
example_credit_candidates_research_only: contributing productive capital to local infrastructure
arkansas_rootedness.feeds: Residual Wealth Contribution design track — not a countable tax-retirement dollar

state_goal_statement: Arkansas should become the easiest place in America to build a family, build a business, build wealth, belong to a community, and participate meaningfully in civic life—whether you live in a city of 200,000 or a town of 2,000.
consequence_rule: If that is built, wealth retention becomes a consequence of prosperity rather than a problem solved with walls

linked_hypotheses.HYP-124: Distributed Arkansas Prosperity Network — specialized connected hubs
linked_hypotheses.HYP-129: Arkansas transition pathway — Layer-1 programs and community wealth
linked_hypotheses.HYP-130: Strategic Capacity Audit — Come Home shortage pipelines
linked_hypotheses.HYP-131: Prosperity-Based Revenue Replacement — External Income + residual wealth sustainability

replacement_stack_role.rule: Do not count hypothetical migration as revenue
replacement_stack_role.note: Appears beside Replacement Stack matrix as sensitivity; not added to countable or primary scenario totals
